title: Multisig signer count scales with the value custodied, and the rule explicitly excludes emergency freeze functions
content:
A.2.11.1.3.2.1.1.2.3.2 sets a hard floor: "[m]ultisigs managing assets with a value equal to or greater than one million USD ($1,000,000) equivalent must have no fewer than seven (7) signers." It then carves out the exception in the same breath — "[t]his requirement applies to custodial control of assets, not emergency freeze functions."

The carve-out is what makes the rule coherent rather than merely strict. Signer count is a collusion cost: seven signers means an attacker must compromise a majority of seven independent parties to steal. That cost is worth paying where value can be moved and worthless where it cannot, since a freeze key controlling a billion dollars of exposure still cannot take a dollar of it.

So the sizing variable is not authority or exposure but *what a compromised key can extract*. This is the same reasoning that exempts emergency-response multisigs from threshold minimums entirely, applied to the other side of the same line.

Note also that a value-indexed requirement is dynamic: a multisig configured compliantly at 900,000 USD becomes non-compliant when the assets it holds appreciate past the threshold, with no action by its administrator. Nothing in the provision assigns responsibility for detecting that crossing, which makes ongoing valuation an implicit administrator duty.
description: Any multisig holding 1,000,000 USD or more must have at least seven signers, but the requirement 'applies to custodial control of assets, not emergency freeze functions'.
